Due to the negligence of “Dr” Iqbal Javaid, I lost one of my budgies this weekend. I noticed my budgies symptoms and quickly started looking for an avian vet. I have never needed to go to the vet before, and did not realize how difficult it would be to find an avian vet in my area. After calling at least a dozen clinics and finally finding one not only nearby, and had an avian vet, but was able to see my bird over the weekend, I quickly prepared my budgie to bring him in to get checked.

When we were called into the exam room and it was time for him to bring my bird out of his carrier, I fully trusted that he was going to be gentle in handling him. I thought I exaggerated things in my mind, or that maybe my bird was just fighting and trying to escape. He was supposedly under the care of a professional. After he checked my bird’s weight, and seeing he was still okay I still trusted he was being gentle in his grip and not hurting him. He soon had my bird back in his hand and placed a towel over him which I thought was to calm him down a bit, but within seconds my bird went from struggling under his grip, then cried out and went silent and still. When I heard his cry I knew he was gone.

He never got as far as an exam, I did not receive a full refund, I did not find out what was wrong with my bird, and I unfortunately did not leave the clinic with my bird still breathing. Instead he continued to tell me how my bird was so weak when I brought him in (he was not) due to my lack of care, and that he unfortunately passed before he could examine him (while holding my bird down the entire time).

Nothing will bring my bird back, but I am sharing in hopes that someone will read and reconsider taking their pet to this clinic. I would hate for anyone to have to experience what we did, but I truly hope this never happens again.
Thank you for the stars we greatly appreciate it.

Absolutely disgusting experience. This place should be shut down.

I came in with my dog after a thunderstorm—he was stumbling, weak, and clearly in distress. I called ahead, and they quoted me $145 just to walk in, without even asking what was going on. That should’ve been the first red flag.

I arrived carrying my dog in my arms, and not a single person looked up or approached us. No urgency. No compassion. Just paperwork and immediate payment—before anyone even laid eyes on my dog. This is supposed to be a medical facility?

We waited about 15 minutes in an empty lobby. A tech took us back and checked his temperature. Then the so called-vet, Iqbal Javaid, DVM, came in, barely did a physical exam, and said he’d be back with a quote. When he returned, he handed me a nearly $800 estimate and still had no clue what was wrong with my dog. No explanation. No effort. Just a giant bill and vague suggestions for tests.

When I took the quote and the vet’s notes to leave, he lost it. Literally shouted at me and tried to snatch the papers out of my hands. I had to RUN out of the clinic with my sick dog in my arms because this unprofessional man was physically trying to take back documents I needed for my records.

I called UrgentVet in Cypress, got seen right away, paid $223 after the exam, plus  full treatment, and —surprise—they actually cared. They checked my dog the moment I walked in, explained everything clearly, and treated him with the urgency he needed. No drama. Just real veterinary care.

How can a place like this be an animal caring facility. Zero compassion, zero ethics, and zero business handling emergencies. If you love your pet, go anywhere else. And if you’ve had a horrible experience like I did—report them.

Staff and Doctor are great.  Because of their work with rescue groups, and it’s privately owned, I’m moving my personal pet care here. They don’t have the swankiest digs, but make up for it in caring service.
